title: When no clean mechanical fix exists for a freshness/staleness gap, declare it as a bounded residual (direction + measured frequency + expiry + pinning test cell) rather than force a fix that trades a rare gap for a systemic cost
decided_by: librarian (codifying a pattern BA/DBA/SecOps converged on twice independently within #56)
content:
OBSERVED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, WITHIN ONE ISSUE (#56, merged b5f6f52), which is what promotes this from a one-off judgment call to a durable project rule.

CASE 1: R7(iii-b) in voice-lint.mjs's turn-boundary fix. The shipped freshness composition is recordMs = max(mtimeMs, Date.parse(updated_at) when finite). This bounds an mtime moved backwards while the record's BYTES were freshly written (an NTP step, an explicit utimes call) because such a record still carries a recent updated_at. It does NOT bound an mtime-PRESERVING restore (cp -p, rsync -a, tar -x): updated_at is file CONTENT, so a verbatim copy carries the OLD updated_at along with the OLD mtime, both terms of max() read stale together, and a record placed on disk this very turn reads as old. A candidate mechanical fix (folding in ctime, which a restore CANNOT preserve in userspace) was seriously evaluated and rejected: ctime is also touched by the project's own deterministic test-fixture-stamping idiom (utimesSync, see testing--voice-lint-fixture-capture-and-mutation-discipline.json), so a ctime-inclusive composition would make every deterministic stale-record test fixture in the suite read as falsely fresh, forcing every one of five affected test cells to be rebuilt on real wall-clock sleeps (~1.1s each, measured) instead of instant deterministic stamps. The residual was declared instead: direction (SILENCE, a missed check, not a false refusal), measured frequency (zero occurrences of cp -p/rsync/tar anywhere under this project's own plugins/ or .github/ trees at spec time), and a pinning test cell (AC16(d)) whose assertion message states its own expiry condition in the assertion text itself: 'if this cell ever exits 2, either a mechanism now dates the record by something a verbatim copy cannot carry, or the fixture no longer constructs the restore signature, and this cell needs a new subject or deletion.'

CASE 2: the existsSync/stat-failure residual (R7 ix) on the same module's resolveStatus explicit-signal branch. A stat failure on a resolved status.json path is guarded to read mtimeMs = +Infinity on throw, so a tooling failure can only ever make a record read maximally fresh (loud), never silence a refusal -- but no code-level fix closes the underlying gap that a PERSISTENT permission fault on that path (not a transient race) genuinely prevents the freshness check from ever running as intended; it is declared, not forced into a workaround that would, per DBA and SecOps's independent Phase 4 finding, still miss one of the two call sites (existsSync vs the statSync catch) reaching the identical silent-drop outcome.

THE RULE, generalised from both cases: when a freshness, staleness, or provenance-trust gap has NO fix that is both (a) mechanically clean and (b) free of a new, larger cost elsewhere (here: breaking the project's own deterministic test-fixture idiom; more generally, this can also be a cost in runtime, in false-positive rate, or in a new attack surface), do not force the fix. Instead: (1) STATE THE FAIL DIRECTION explicitly (does the gap produce a false refusal, a silence, or a wrong value -- see evidence.md's directional-defect rule; a silence and a false refusal are NOT interchangeable and must never be described as 'the same kind of gap'). (2) MEASURE the frequency or exposure at the point of decision, with its window stated, even if the honest answer is zero-observed -- a declared-zero is a real measurement, not an excuse to skip measuring. (3) WRITE THE EXPIRY CONDITION -- the specific future fact (a new mechanism, a new observed occurrence, a vendor change) that would re-open the question -- INTO the artifact that will outlive the decision: the module's own header comment AND, where the project has one, a test assertion message that fires if the residual's premise ever stops holding. (4) PIN IT WITH A TEST CELL that asserts the CURRENT declared behaviour (not the absence of a fix), so the residual is a documented, observable fact about the shipped system rather than an untested gap that silently drifts.

WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT JUST DILIGENCE: the tempting alternative in both cases was to keep pushing for 'one more mechanism' (ctime; a broader existsSync/statSync unification) until the gap closed to zero. Both times, the actual next mechanism considered would have traded a residual with zero observed occurrences for a certain, systemic cost (a slower and flakier test suite; in the general case this could as easily be a broader attack surface or a higher false-positive rate elsewhere). The declared-bounded-residual is the record of having made that trade consciously, with its cost stated, rather than either shipping silently undocumented or over-engineering against a threat with no measured basis.
